subject: Guardrail validation & dedicated capacity recommendation for NeoMed (performance / SLOs)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Lin <alex.lin@neomed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-06T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + data we need for performance validation

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and the actionable items we discussed so we can size a dedicated capacity pilot and validate SLOs.

Call recap (brief):
- NeoMed goal: low-latency streaming for clinical summarization + high-concurrency inference for batch triage.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 latency for non-streaming endpoints around ~150ms; streaming tail (p99) under ~300ms end-to-end. Peak concurrent active sessions estimated at ~180.
- Key unknowns: average response length (tokens), prompt variability, and whether KV/prefix caching will apply to large cohorts.

What we need from you to produce a benchable pilot & recommendation (requested items):
1) Sample prompt set: 500-1,000 representative prompts (anonymized) or a short dataset spreadsheet with expected token lengths.
2) Traffic profile: expected peak qps/concurrency windows (5‑minute peak, 1‑hour peak) and percentiles (p50/p95).
3) Example streaming session: typical message chunk size and final message size (tokens).
4) Any regulatory constraints (data retention, on-prem routing) that would impact caching or dedicated Private deployment.

Preliminary hypotheses (what we'll validate):
- GPU choices: H100 will provide the best latency/throughput headroom for large-context streaming; A100 gives good cost-throughput balance; L4 may be cost-effective for smaller models or high-quantization workloads but struggles with long-context streaming.
- Concurrency sizing: for a 13B-class model quantized to 4-bit, expect ~20–28 concurrent streaming sessions per H100 with sustained token throughput; reserve multiple GPUs for headroom and failover.
- Reserved throughput vs. requests: We'll size both reserved GPU pool and a throughput cap (tokens/sec) so you get predictable p95 latency while avoiding unnecessary over-provisioning.

Next steps / timeline:
- You: share sample prompts + traffic profile by EOD Wed (2028-08-08).
- Us: we’ll produce a bench plan and two concrete capacity options (Cost-optimized and Performance-optimized) within 48 hours of receiving the input. That plan will include: exact GPU matrix to test (A100/H100/L4), quantization settings, concurrency targets, and a 24‑hour pilot schedule.

Attachments: I’ve included a one-page bench checklist (bench_plan.xlsx) and a suggested JSON schema for the sample prompts.

If this aligns, I’ll route to Ben to scope an ops checklist and to Lauren to tentatively schedule the pilot kickoff.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference — Inference you can measure
From: Alex Lin <alex.lin@neomed.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@neomed.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-07T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + data we need for performance validation

Thanks Priyom — that looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Quick answers and a couple clarifications:

1) Traffic / tokens
- Peak concurrent sessions: 180 (5‑minute rolling).
- Average request: ~120 tokens in prompts, responses average ~350 tokens when summarizing long notes (streamed).
- We also have nightly batch workloads (bulk triage) that hit throughput but are OK with higher latency.

2) Streaming behavior
- Important: streaming must start delivering first chunks within 120–150ms on p95 to our front-end to keep our UX snappy; final p99 tail can be up to 350ms in worst cases.

3) Security / retention
- Standard BAAs in place; data cannot be stored in unmanaged caches beyond 24 hours unless explicitly approved.

Attached: customer_usecase.pdf (short product flow + a couple of sample transcripts). We’ll try to export 500 anonymized prompts by Wednesday.

Open question: how aggressive are your quantization recommendations for streaming? We’ve seen 4-bit configs that affect token times — curious how much delta you expect vs FP16 for the streaming tail.

If you want, schedule a short 30‑minute working session tomorrow for Ben/your infra folks to walk through the bench checklist.

—
Alex Lin
Head of Platform | NeoMed AI
alex.lin@neomed.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Lin <alex.lin@neomed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + data we need for performance validation

Alex — perfect, thanks for the details and the PDF. Notes below + our recommended pilot matrix and immediate next steps.

Short answers to your open question on quantization impact:
- Expect 4‑bit quantization to reduce GPU memory and increase throughput significantly, but with a latency delta of ~5–12% on token generation compared to FP16 in our internal benches (depends on model family and kernel support). For streaming where first-chunk latency matters, we recommend testing both FP16 and 4-bit in the pilot for a subset of prompts.

Pilot recommendation (two-track):
- Option A — Performance-optimized (H100):
  • Hardware: 3 x H100 (reserved pool)
  • Config: FP16 for warm path; 4-bit for lower-cost fallback variants
  • Expected sustained: ~26 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU for your 13–70B candidate models; total ~78 concurrent with headroom -> meets 180 with autoscale/burst planning across zones
  • Reserved throughput target: 140k tokens/sec (cluster-wide)
  • When to pick: when first-chunk latency / tail is critical.

- Option B — Cost-balanced (A100 + mixed quantized lineup):
  • Hardware: 4 x A100 (reserved)
  • Config: 4-bit quantization for majority; perfume FP16 for the small subset of very latency-sensitive endpoints
  • Expected sustained: ~18–24 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU depending on model size; reserve concurrency 60–96 and add short-burst capacity
  • Reserved throughput target: 110k tokens/sec
  • When to pick: when cost predicts higher importance and some latency slack is acceptable.

- Option C — Lightweight / Experimental (L4 for smaller models):
  • Hardware: 6 x L4 (reserved) for small LLMs and high-concurrency low-latency cheap paths
  • Caveat: streaming tail and very long contexts (>8k tokens) will degrade; use only for specific non-critical endpoints.

Operational guardrails we’ll include in the pilot:
- Autoscale triggers: queue depth + p95 latency smoothing window.
- Fallback policy: on latency breach, route to a lower-cost variant (quantized or smaller model) with throttles & user-visible degrade message.
- Monitoring: per-route p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.

Deliverables after sample data:
- 48-hour bench report (A100 vs H100 vs L4) with p50/p95/p99 numbers for both streaming-first-chunk and total completion latency.
- Cost estimate (monthly reserved + expected overage) for each option.
- Pilot runbook and rollback plan.

Can Ben and I book the 30‑minute ops working session at 2pm PT today? If that time doesn’t work, share two alternative 30‑minute windows and Lauren will lock it in.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
